newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says ailing President Anh recovering.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says ailing President Anh recovering.

text.p: Vietnamese President Le Duc Anh's health is improving, the foreign ministry said on Tuesday in response to reports that he was critically ill after suffering a brain haemorrhage. "According to information we have just received, President Le Duc Anh is in the process of health recovery," a ministry spokesman said in a one-sentence statement.

The statement was a response to inquiries about reports that Anh, one of the communist country's leadership troika, had been seriously incapacitated by a brain haemorrhage and would not recover sufficiently, if at all, to resume his duties.
Political and diplomatic sources told Reuters on Tuesday that Anh had been in a coma and breathing with the aid of a respirator at the Hanoi 108 Army Hospital.
"He won't be going back to his job, that's sure," said one.
It was not clear if, by recovery, the foreign ministry meant he had now regained consciousness.
The government last week admitted, in a passing reference in official media reports, that Anh was unwell.
But until now, the only official comment on his predicament had come from the foreign ministry, which said he was "tired" and in need of a rest.

Anh, who holds a key position of influence over the military and security apparatus, is part of leadership triumvirate that includes Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi, 79, and reformist Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, 74.
According to the constitution, the vice president must stand in if the president is incapacitated for a long period.

Anh's deputy, Nguyen Thi Binh, is not a member of the Politburo or the party's Central Committee. As such she would be expected to play only a figurehead role until a successor is chosen and then put to the National Assembly for approval.
Analysts say Anh's departure could reopen an internal debate over leadership succession that had simmered ahead of a key Communist Party congress earlier this year.

Muoi, Anh and Kiet represent a balance of different political hues within the party and come from the north, the centre and the south of the country. Analysts say Anh is considered to be the most conservative of the three.

Sources said four senior Politburo members, National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh, Defence Minister General Doan Khue, Lieutenant-General Le Kha Phieu and Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam were likely candidates to replace Anh.
